description: A fixed-length dataset whose record carries a table one of whose items is redefined twice, read noodoslide -- a constant four entries, the count an ordinary item beside them. Nothing in the record says which alternative an entry carries: entry one is a home address, entries two and three are work addresses and entry four is a mailing address, and that rule is written in the layout as a schedule over the positions rather than as a predicate over any item's bytes. A consumer that looked for a discriminating byte would find none, and one that took the first arm for the whole table would read a work entry's desk out of a home entry's state. The work arm is three bytes shorter than the run it redefines, so it carries a slack run no item covers, once per occupied position -- which here is the descriptor's fact rather than the data's: every record of this file carries two such runs, at the same two offsets. ADR-TAIL is behind the table and holds the record's length to account, so a dropped slack run, or a table read at the count rather than at the fixed four, moves it. The count says two in the second record and the table still holds four entries, which is what makes the reading visible.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "An arm may be selected by its position in the table", "A variant is chosen once per occurrence", "What the descriptor determines, a writer supplies", "Members never overlap, and `REDEFINES` is resolved away", "Slack is a node, not a rule", "Slack survives a read" and "An item after a table slides, and the other reading is a fixed table"; docs/layout/SPEC.md, "A schedule for a redefine chosen by position", "The `OCCURS DEPENDING ON` reading is one statement per layout" and "lrecl and blksize describe the dataset, not the stream"; the alphanumeric bytes and the storage widths are cobol-go codec/SPEC.md, "Storage Widths" and "Group items, OCCURS, and SYNCHRONIZED". That the retained slack is the same bytes is not something a values document can state; see the corpus README.
